title: Foundations of Clinical Informatics
summary: What clinical informatics is, where it sits next to the other informatics subfields, the data → information → knowledge → wisdom hierarchy, the short history of how we got here, and Friedman's fundamental theorem.
learningOutcomes: Define clinical informatics and locate it precisely against bioinformatics, public health informatics, and consumer health informatics.
Walk the data-information-knowledge-wisdom hierarchy with a clinical example at each level.
Tell the short history of clinical informatics from the Lockheed Hospital Information System to the post-Meaningful-Use era.
State and apply Friedman's fundamental theorem of biomedical informatics.
Explain why informatics is not just 'IT in healthcare' in a way a CMO would accept.
